docs.description: Icon-only action button. 108 variants: size (sm 32px, md 40px, lg 48px) × shape (square, round) × prio (primary, secondary, tertiary) × state (default, hover, pressed, focus, loading, disabled). Drawn heights are the visible control; the 44×44px WCAG hit area is padded in code (no target-size variable exists yet). Mirrors the Button priority/size/state system using SOLAR action tokens; the duplicate state=active was removed on 2026-09-23 — use pressed. An icon-only control must carry an aria-label — the icon alone is not a name.

rules.reason: The closest stock control on each platform. MUI IconButton takes loading and disabled and supplies focus handling and keyboard activation; Flutter's IconButton takes a ButtonStyle, as FilledButton does for Button, so the same style builder restyles it.
As Button, whose API names it `variant`; `prio` is the Figma property name.

Drawn as Figma draws it. Primary has a 1px border at sm, at rest, in focus and while loading, and none on hover, press or disable, nor at md or lg; secondary has one at sm and md in every state, and tertiary none. So the border depends on priority and state as well as size. Button keeps its border in every state, which is raised with SOLAR.
What the shape axis is for: square takes radius.control and round radius.pill, at every size, priority and state.

As Button (owner decision 2026-09-23 for its lg): drawn as Figma draws it. lg is flat, keeping only the focus ring, so the shadow depends on size as well as on the paint axes. Figma also rings a pressed primary or secondary at sm and md, where Button keeps its control shadow; followed here, and raised with SOLAR.
Same values, governed tokens, one step of the icon ladder per size; the icon's height is already bound to them.

As Button: SOLAR publishes no control height token (owner decision 2026-09-23, raised as a governance gap). Drawn 32, 40 and 48; the description's 28, 36 and 44 disagree, which the design review lists (section 3, described sizes).
An icon button is square, so its width is its height, under the same decision.
As at md, the border width is 0 at lg, so the colour is never drawn.

Primary draws a 1px color.border.medium border at sm and none at md, so the colour Figma leaves off at md is never drawn; the border width, which follows size, priority and state, carries the difference. The inconsistency with Button's primary border is raised with SOLAR.
